dataset.license: UCI dataset record; verify attribution/terms for redistribution
dataset.name: Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits (scikit-learn copy)

experiment: FP32 versus STE-binarized hidden layers on UCI handwritten digits
limitations: The sklearn digits set is a small 8x8 benchmark, not a modern vision workload.
The binary network is not fully integer: biases and final layer stay FP32; training uses FP32 straight-through gradients.
Python big-integer popcount is a correctness backend, not optimized SIMD/native code; its measured latency is implementation-specific.
Three seeds and one fixed split are an exploratory comparison, not a broad accuracy estimate.

method.binary_inference: Python integer XNOR/popcount for two hidden layers; FP32 final layer
method.binary_model: 64-128-64 binary hidden layers trained with straight-through sign; FP32 output layer
method.float_model: 64-128-64-10 ReLU MLP, FP32 weights and activations
method.input_binarization: threshold normalized pixel intensities at 8 on the original 0..16 scale
method.split: stratified 75/25 split, random_state=4107, shared across models
